text:
Soojin Lee: Hey team — quick ask for the reference program. We have 3 case study drafts in review (Arcadia Health / QuantaPay / NovaDocs) and we need a few volunteers to do a *technical accuracy + positioning consistency* pass.

Soojin Lee: Looking for ~30–45 mins each. Even if you only review one story, that helps a lot.

Soojin Lee: What to look for:
- Are we describing the deployment mode correctly (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)?
- Any product naming drift (Console / Optimize / rollouts / fallbacks)?
- Claims language: anything that sounds like we’re over-promising or implying a hard SLA we don’t have
- Metrics phrasing: does it clearly state measurement window + baseline vs post-Redwood?
- Architecture diagram callouts: anything that’s misleading / missing key constraints
- Security wording: anything that could trip security review (esp. Arcadia)

Soojin Lee: Drafts (internal-only links):
- Arcadia (Private/VPC): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RedwoodInternalArcadiaDraft
- QuantaPay (Dedicated): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RedwoodInternalQuantaPayDraft
- NovaDocs (Hosted + Optimize): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RedwoodInternalNovaDocsDraft

Soojin Lee: If you can help, reply with which one(s) you’ll take + by when. Targeting comments by EOD tomorrow so we can turn customer review around this week.

Camila Reyes: +1 — we specifically need eyes on the “outcomes” sections. We’ve had a few internal debates on how to state latency/cost wins without sounding absolute.

Ethan Wallace: For reviewers: comments directly in the doc are best. If you want to just drop bullets here, also fine — I’ll transcribe into the comment log.

Markus Klein: I can take QuantaPay. Mostly want to ensure we’re not mixing “Dedicated capacity” with “private deployment” language + the burst behavior wording is accurate.

Soojin Lee: @Markus Klein awesome, thank you. Biggest red-flag area there is the p95 numbers + what traffic shape that benchmark reflects.

Simran Kaur: I’ll review Arcadia. Will sanity-check the VPC/private control plane description + anything about KMS/key ownership + audit logs.

Naomi Feldman: I can do a quick security/claims scan on Arcadia too (15–20 mins). Please make sure we’re not referencing any specific compliance artifacts (like “SOC 2 report provided”) in a way that reads like it’s customer-facing.

Simran Kaur: @Naomi Feldman perfect — I’ll tag you on the paragraphs that feel borderline.

Logan Wright: I’ll take NovaDocs outcomes section. Want to verify the “cost per query” math isn’t conflating embeddings + rerank tokens. If there’s a source dashboard link, drop it in.

Ben Carter: FYI the docs site case-studies section is landing early next week. If you leave feedback on CTA language / headings, we can incorporate before publish.

Tessa Morgan: I’ll review the visuals + diagrams across all three (layout + labeling). If anyone sees a diagram that needs a stronger “illustrative” disclaimer, tag me.

Miguel Santos: Adding CS perspective: please flag anything that sounds like “we did it for them” vs “they implemented with Redwood.” Some customers are sensitive to that.

Jordan Blake: Thanks all. One more note: keep the positioning tight — production economics + reliability + deployment flexibility. If we say “best latency” or “cheapest,” we’ll get dragged into benchmark wars.

Soojin Lee: Appreciate everyone jumping in.

Soojin Lee: Quick guardrails reminder:
- Don’t add customer-specific identifiers beyond what’s already in the draft (assume these could get forwarded)
- If you suggest new metrics, also suggest *how we’d validate them* (window + data source)

Slackbot: Reminder: Please avoid sharing sensitive customer information in #general. Use approved internal docs and follow the customer communications policy.
